title: 2026 AMC 8 Problem 17
statement: Four students are seated in a row. They chat with the people sitting next to them, then rearrange themselves so that they are no longer seated next to any of the same people. How many rearrangements are possible?

solutions.text: Name the original order \(A,B,C,D\). The forbidden neighboring pairs are \(AB\), \(BC\), and \(CD\), so the only allowed pairs are \(AC\), \(AD\), and \(BD\). To seat all four students in a row, the three row-adjacencies must be exactly these three edges, giving \(C,A,D,B\) or its reverse. There are \(2\) rearrangements.
hints: The allowed neighboring pairs are \(AC\), \(AD\), and \(BD\)
